Associate Product Director at Novo NordiskGenAI proof of concept for automating compliance reviews
Agentic RAG proof of concept for compliance reviews, with a Figma plugin		Every release of health software needed sign-off from medical, legal and regulatory reviewers. The process was built for marketing materials, not software: every screen was manually captured as a PDF and reviewed manually, stacking the regulatory risk to the end of the development cycle and sometimes adding months to delivery.Test whether an LLM could take on the review so product teams could shift left: fail in design, not at review. Two acceptance tests set up front: useful to product teams, and catches what the manual review catches.Used an internal LLM sandbox to build a RAG model over the guidelines and regulations, producing a full audit trail per submission. Built a prototype agent that plugged into Figma so designers could query the guidelines before investing effort. Pitched it to senior leadership.First test passed: product teams used the Figma plugin on real designs and loved it. The second never ran: a reorg and a vendor contract took the use case, the work went to another team, and Tom moved to the Wegovy Pill launch. The proof of concept showed a clear path to much faster release cycles.Feb 2022 - Feb 2026AI, GenAI, regulated, compliance, pharma, healthcare, discovery, prototyping, ways of working, launch, marketing, team leadership, stakeholders

Wegovycare weight-loss prediction model		Patient research showed everyone wanted the same three things: how much weight they will lose, whether this is normal, whether they are on track. TomBot, a chatbot CV at takenbyninjas.com		Recruiters are bored of conventional CVs, and Tom wanted to find out first-hand what AI can and cannot do.
